drafts.title: Front seats provide longer thigh support and reliable memory recall
drafts.description: Front seat gives taller drivers measurable additional thigh support and restores saved seat positions reliably so drivers do not have to readjust after switching drivers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Power-adjustable thigh support provides at least 60 mm of additional forward support compared with the current 5 Series front cushion midpoint (i.e., a dedicated extension range >= 60 mm), and the seat memory restores saved driver position within ±10 mm linear position and ±1° angular position in at least 9 out of 10 consecutive recalls.
assumptions: A 60 mm additional extension meaningfully improves comfort for drivers in the >95th percentile height range (tall drivers).
Seat actuator resolution and sensors available on the successor can achieve ±10 mm / ±1° repeatability.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort varies by body shape; some users may need more than 60 mm.
Long-term wear could affect memory repeatability.

drafts.title: Rear seating offers competitor-class legroom
drafts.description: Rear occupants experience legroom that matches or exceeds main competitors, ensuring adults can sit behind tall front occupants without feeling cramped.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear knee-to-seatback clearance (ISO seating reference method) is >= 980 mm in the standard rear bench position for the vehicle, matching or exceeding key rivals (e.g., mainstream E-segment competitors) in internal benchmark tests.
assumptions: Competitor benchmark average rear legroom is approximately 975 mm; the 980 mm target places the successor at or above that level.
Measurement uses a consistent ISO or OEM-defined seating reference point across vehicles.
uncertainties: Rivals may change packaging in their next refresh before the successor launches.
Different body sizes and seating recline configurations affect perceived legroom.

drafts.title: Cup holders accept common bottle sizes and secure them during normal driving
drafts.description: Cup holders accommodate commonly used beverage containers and hold them securely so bottles and cups do not tip or rattle during typical maneuvers.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accept cylindrical containers up to 90 mm diameter and 300 mm height and retain them without tipping under longitudinal or lateral accelerations up to 0.5 g in lab tests.
assumptions: Common single-use and reusable bottles for the US market are typically below 90 mm in diameter.
0.5 g is a reasonable test proxy for brisk lane changes and moderate emergency braking events.
uncertainties: Some oversized containers (e.g., wide travel mugs) may still not fit.
Aftermarket bottle shapes may behave differently than standard cylinders.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on the first attempt
drafts.description: Customers can open the hands-free tailgate with a single gesture and expect it to open promptly without repeated attempts under normal conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens on the first valid user gesture within 1.5 seconds in at least 90% of attempts across tested ambient conditions from -10 °C to +40 °C and with the key fob present within 0.5–1.5 m of the rear bumper.
assumptions: Typical user gestures and fob positions fall within the stated distance range.
Environmental interference (e.g., heavy dirt/snow on sensors) is excluded from the base test and handled as a separate durability case.
uncertainties: Very heavy mud/ice or blocked sensors may still cause failures.
Different footwear or gait styles could affect detection in edge cases.

drafts.title: Exterior door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Customers can open the doors with the flush handles in winter conditions; handles do not remain stuck due to icing in normal cold-weather use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles operate successfully in at least 95% of controlled freeze-thaw cycles down to -20 °C in lab tests representative of typical winter exposure (100 cycles), and users can open the door on first attempt in these conditions.
assumptions: -20 °C covers the typical low-temperature range encountered by most US cold-weather customers.
Test cycles simulate common freeze, thaw, and refreeze patterns seen in customer use.
uncertainties: Extreme salt, heavy debris, or aftermarket sealants could still cause adhesion or freezing beyond tested conditions.
Very rare, extreme arctic conditions may exceed the test envelope.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting with a wide color palette and granular brightness control
drafts.description: Drivers and passengers can personalize cabin ambient lighting with many colors and fine brightness steps so interior mood and visibility fit their preferences.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting provides at least 64 selectable colors and a minimum of 10 distinct brightness steps per lighting zone, with per-zone control (front doors, rear doors, dash, footwell) available in the vehicle UI.
assumptions: Customers perceive a 64-color palette and 10 brightness steps as a noticeable increase in personalization over current offerings.
Per-zone control is limited to practical cabin zones (front/rear/doors/dash/footwell).
uncertainties: Some customers prefer physical controls over deep UI menus for color selection.
Color perception varies with interior materials and ambient daylight.

drafts.title: Trunk provides a powered outlet usable for a portable cooler
drafts.description: Customers can plug and run common portable coolers from a socket inside the trunk without needing to run cables through the cabin or fold seats.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A dedicated trunk power outlet is provided inside the cargo area and can operate a typical 40 W portable cooler continuously for 2 hours in a standard vehicle-off test without error.
assumptions: A 40 W cooler represents a common portable cooler power draw for customer use cases.
Vehicle electrical architecture permits accessory power in the trunk with proper safety measures.
uncertainties: Extended operation (many hours) may be limited by vehicle safety/power policies when the vehicle is off.
Some high-draw aftermarket coolers may exceed the outlet capability.

drafts.title: Front-end design meets new EU pedestrian protection regulation (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers requested that the vehicle front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle front-end design must demonstrate compliance with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation as required by homologation authorities.
assumptions: This is a regulation-driven requirement requiring engineering and homologation work beyond product-level feature design.
uncertainties: Final regulation text and test procedures may change prior to homologation deadlines.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance / homologation requirement; out of product-level scope for customer-facing feature definition.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification (certification request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Rear-seat airbag system must meet FMVSS 208 certification criteria as required for vehicles sold under that regulation.
assumptions: FMVSS 208 is a certification/regulatory target and requires engineering and testing to certify rather than a pure customer feature.
uncertainties: Certification timelines and test procedures may change and differ by region.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory / certification requirement; out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern follows ECE R112 rules where applicable (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Headlamp assemblies/aiming meet the ECE R112 beam pattern requirements for markets that require ECE R112 compliance.
assumptions: ECE R112 is a regulatory/technical standard and compliance is part of homologation for markets that require it.
uncertainties: Markets have different headlight standards (ECE vs. FMVSS), requiring region-specific solutions.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance / homologation; engineering-level requirement rather than a customer-facing outcome.

drafts.title: Volume knob magnetic encoder request (component-level specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested that the volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component specification: volume control uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder as a supplier engineering requirement.
assumptions: This is a component-level engineering specification rather than a direct customer-experience requirement.
uncertainties: Customer-visible benefit (e.g., tactile feel, resolution) depends on UI integration and control logic, not just encoder bits.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/component specification; out of scope for customer-facing requirement definition.

drafts.title: Side window glass thickness specification request (component-level)
drafts.description: Customers requested that side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component-level specification: side windows constructed from 4.5 mm laminated glass per customer request.
assumptions: Glass thickness is an engineering/materials decision that impacts NVH and safety but is a component-level spec.
uncertainties: Trade-offs between weight, NVH, cost and regulatory side-impact selection of glass thickness.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/material specification; out of product-level customer-facing scope.

drafts.title: Seat foam density request (component-level specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested component-level target: seat cushion foam specified at 55 kg/m³ density.
assumptions: Foam density is a materials/engineering specification; the customer outcome is improved perceived comfort which should be validated separately.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort depends on foam formulation, layering and cover materials, not density alone.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/material specification; out of scope for direct customer-facing requirement drafting.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business/financial request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer-requested business guarantee: 60% residual value after five years (requested), to be evaluated by corporate finance and sales programs.
assumptions: Residual value guarantees are a commercial/financial program decision, not a technical product feature.
uncertainties: Guaranteeing residuals depends on market conditions, resale programs and business viability.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/financial request (price/residual guarantees); out of scope for product-feature requirements.

drafts.title: Production cost reduction request (business/cost target)
drafts.description: Customers requested that BMW cut production cost per car by 8%.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Requested business-level target: reduce production cost per vehicle by 8% compared with prior model year baseline.
assumptions: Production cost targets are internal business/industrial engineering objectives and not a customer-facing functional requirement.
uncertainties: Achieving cost targets depends on supplier contracts, volume, and corporate cost programs.
drafts.scope_reason: Business / cost target; out of scope for customer-facing product requirement drafting.
